failure_injection_retry.executed_on: 2026-09-08 against PostgreSQL 16.13 with the real FastAPI app and TestClient

class_a_failure_before_business_commit.evidence: each injected first request returned 500 and rolled back; the same-key retry then succeeded (201 reservation / 200 issue) and produced exactly one clinical effect and one inventory movement
class_a_failure_before_business_commit.receipt_evidence: added in Phase 14C: after the successful retry exactly 1 clinical_command_receipts row exists with status completed, proving the rolled-back claim left no orphan receipt

class_b_failure_after_business_commit.scenario: failure injected immediately after db.commit(), modelling a committed business transaction whose response never reaches the client
class_b_failure_after_business_commit.first_response: 500; the effect is nonetheless durably committed
class_b_failure_after_business_commit.retry_response: 409 with the canonical safe envelope code CONFLICT; the existing replay contract, no new API contract was invented
class_b_failure_after_business_commit.business_effect: exactly 1 reservation / exactly 1 issue (fulfilled_units=1, unit status issued); unchanged by the retry
class_b_failure_after_business_commit.inventory_movement: exactly 1 movement of the relevant type for the lab; unchanged by the retry
class_b_failure_after_business_commit.idempotency_claims: exactly 1 clinical_command_receipts row with status completed both before and after the retry
class_b_failure_after_business_commit.fingerprint: the stored request fingerprint is identical before and after the retry
class_b_failure_after_business_commit.partial_state: no partial or orphan state: lab-wide counts of reservations, issued units and movements all remain 1

failure_injection_retry.mechanism: test-only and gated by ENV=test, RUNTIME_MODE=test, an explicit GULA_TEST_FAILURE_STAGE value, and a stage allowlist; Phase 14C added the after_commit stage to that same allowlist and one maybe_fail call after the commit in the reservation and issue routes
failure_injection_retry.production_safety: no production bypass, no suppressed exception, no weakened validation; the 27 pre-existing Blood Bank tests run through the same routes with no failure stage set and still pass

wave1_lifecycle_e2e.path: POST /blood-bank/reservations -> GET /blood-bank/units/{id}/traceability -> POST /blood-bank/reservations/{id}/release -> GET traceability, against real PostgreSQL with the real FastAPI app, real auth/authorisation and the real clinical command guard

completed_replay_response.result: verified by existing Phase 14B/14B.1/14C evidence; no retest performed
completed_replay_response.behaviour: a completed command replayed under the same Idempotency-Key returns a deterministic 409 with the canonical safe envelope code CONFLICT and creates no second effect
covered_by: post-commit retry for reservation and issue (14C)
completed_replay_response.design_note: the original 2xx response payload is deliberately not persisted and not replayed; the contract is a deterministic conflict, not a stored-response replay. Stored-response replay is an enhancement, not a Wave 1 gap.

state_machine_duplicate_key_fix.defect: app/blood_bank/domain/state_machine.py declared the key "reserved" twice in the single _TRANSITIONS table shared by all Blood Bank entities. The later order-lifecycle entry silently shadowed the blood-unit entry, so reserved -> available and reserved -> released were rejected and a reserved unit could never be returned to the available pool.
state_machine_duplicate_key_fix.discovered_by: the Wave 1 lifecycle E2E: POST /blood-bank/reservations/{id}/release returned 422 'Invalid blood_unit transition: reserved -> available'
state_machine_duplicate_key_fix.fix: merged the two sets into one "reserved" entry and removed the duplicate key; no redesign, no other transition changed
state_machine_duplicate_key_fix.audit: an AST scan of _TRANSITIONS confirms 38 keys, 38 unique, no remaining shadowed key
state_machine_duplicate_key_fix.residual_risk: the table remains entity-agnostic, so the merged set is the union of the unit and order transitions and is slightly wider for orders. Per-entity keying is the correct structural fix and is deferred to a later Blood Bank hardening wave.

not_verified.full_backend_regression: DEFERRED to the platform-wide regression wave. Not required for Wave 1: the Phase 14C production change is confined to the Blood Bank routes plus one entry in the test-only failure-injection allowlist, and the Phase 14D change is confined to the Blood Bank state machine. maybe_fail call sites are only the Blood Bank routes and the shared guard's pre-existing after_audit_preparation stage, so there is no cross-domain impact. The 32-test Blood Bank suite is the narrower sufficient regression.
not_verified.production_dependency_remediation: SPLIT in Phase 14D: signxml is not a Wave 1 production blocker (see blocked.signxml_lock_gap); the Alembic head state IS a Wave 1 production blocker (see blocked.alembic_multiple_heads_blocks_fresh_deploy).
not_verified.general_clinical_audit_chain_concurrency: DEFERRED to the global Audit/Security/Integrity wave. blocked.clinical_command_receipts_lineage: BLOCKED: clinical_command_receipts, the durable idempotency claim table, is created only by migration 20260819_0003_clinical_command_receipts, which sits on a different Alembic head from the Blood Bank lineage. Upgrading to 20260901_0004 alone leaves the table absent and every guarded Blood Bank write fails with UndefinedTable. The verification database required that migration's own DDL to be applied separately. Root cause is the pre-existing duplicate revision id 20260819_0003 and the unrelated multiple-head state, which are out of scope for this phase and were not modified.
blocked.requirements_lock_missing_signxml: BLOCKED for lock-only installs: signxml>=4.2.0 is declared in backend/requirements.txt but absent from backend/requirements-lock.txt, so an environment built from the lock file alone cannot import app.security.saml_service and therefore cannot start the application. Documented only; the dependency manifests were not modified in this phase.
blocked.alembic_upgrade_head: pre-existing duplicate revision 20260819_0003 and unrelated multiple heads; unchanged
blocked.github_actions_artifact_quota: BLOCKED and unchanged: the GitHub Actions artifact storage quota is exhausted account-wide, failing several CI jobs purely at the upload-artifact step. This session has no permission to re-run failed jobs (403 Resource not accessible by integration). Not investigated further in Phase 14C.
blocked.frontend_mobile_bottom_nav_test: BLOCKED and unchanged: a pre-existing failing test in frontend-v3/src/components/navigation/MobileBottomNav.test.tsx, unrelated to the Blood Bank work and untouched by this branch.
blocked.alembic_multiple_heads_blocks_fresh_depl: BLOCKER for Wave 1 production operation, executed evidence, not fixed in this phase. On a clean PostgreSQL database both 'alembic upgrade head' and 'alembic upgrade heads' FAIL and create no tables at all: head fails with 'Multiple head revisions are present', heads fails with 'Requested revision 20260819_0004 overlaps with other requested revisions 20260819_0003'. alembic heads reports three heads (20260819_0004, 20260820_0005, 20260901_0004) and warns 'Revision 20260819_0003 is present more than once'. Consequence: a fresh deploy cannot create clinical_command_receipts, the table every guarded Blood Bank write depends on. Root cause is the pre-existing duplicate revision id and multiple-head state, explicitly out of scope for phases 14B-14D. Wave 1 must not be certified for production until this is remediated.
blocked.signxml_lock_gap: NOT a Wave 1 production blocker. Both backend/Dockerfile and the root Dockerfile install from backend/requirements.txt, which declares signxml>=4.2.0, so the production image builds correctly. The gap affects only environments built from backend/requirements-lock.txt. Deferred to platform dependency hardening.
